answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a refundable stake bonded in escrow, like basalt bedrock under a harbor: registering is cheap, but becoming useful is expensive, because the stake only unlocks after sustained honest work. Every new identity enters through a narrow inlet of low-trust jobs — small escrowed tasks and peer review — and only a long record of completed work widens it. An attacker spinning up thousands of shale-thin fake identities must fund each bond and wait out the same slow trust build-up, so the cost scales with the attack while honest agents pay it once.
